audit_findings.title: Owner earnings may treat reserve releases as durable earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $18.7 million pretax in 2025, equal to 48.2% of $38.8 million 2025 OE; $18.5 million pretax in 2024; favorable adjustments fell to $3.1 million in H1 2026 from $12.6 million in H1 2025
audit_findings.mechanism: Prior-accident-year liability and premium adjustments reduce workers’ compensation expense and therefore increase reported earnings and the historical OE series used to set the $38.3 million anchor.
audit_findings.evidence: The estimate we recorded for workers’ compensation costs was reduced by $18.7 million and $18.5 million in 2025 and 2024, respectively, due to changes in estimated losses for prior accident years.
audit_findings.explanation: The reserve benefits and their inclusion in reported operating results are demonstrated, while their exact inclusion in calculated OE and sustainable portion remain unresolved. Their scale is large relative to the anchor, and the sharp reduction in favorable adjustments during 2026 shows that assuming the 2024-2025 level continues could materially overstate normalized OE and every scenario value.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile each OE year to current-accident-year costs, prior-period liability development, and return-premium adjustments; establish a repeatable normalized component, remove any nonrecurring portion from the anchor, and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Cash added to equity value may be required operating liquidity
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; the tested bridge amount is $67.889 million, or $2.55 per diluted share and 11.2% of the $606 million base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: The bridge adds all cash and short-term investments to operating value; any amount needed for payroll cycles, taxes, benefits, claims, premiums, collateral, or client-payment timing is operating capital rather than distributable excess cash.
audit_findings.evidence: These obligations are fixed whether or not the client makes payments to us as required by our services agreement.
audit_findings.explanation: The operating-liquidity requirement is demonstrated by BBSI’s fixed payroll obligations, but the distributable residual is not established. At June 30, 2026, BBSI had $407.885 million of current liabilities, including $272.487 million of accrued payroll and benefits, against $67.889 million of cash and unrestricted investments, and used $77.954 million of operating cash in H1 2026. Those figures do not prove that none of the cash is excess, but they make the full $67.889 million addition materially unsupported.
audit_findings.action: Build a June 2026 liquidity waterfall covering receivables timing, accrued payroll, payroll taxes, benefits, premiums, claims, customer deposits, collateral, and peak payroll-cycle funding; rerun the bridge using only the demonstrated distributable residual.

audit_findings.title: Unreserved IRS claim is absent from the equity bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $11.565 million recorded net loss impact, or $0.43 per diluted share and 1.9% of $606 million base equity value; adding the unrecorded $1.8 million penalties gives $13.365 million, or $0.50 per share and 2.2% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: The tax judgment is a nonrecurring claim on common equity that must enter either OE or the equity bridge; if still unpaid, adding gross cash without recognizing the related obligation overstates equity value.
audit_findings.evidence: BBSI received notices that the IRS intends to disallow certain wage-based tax credits claimed for the years 2017 through 2021 , which could result in estimated total additional taxes of $ 8.0 million and penalties and interest of $ 5.2 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The 10-K premise that no reserve existed is superseded by the June 2026 10-Q: after an adverse Tax Court decision, BBSI recorded $8.6 million of tax expense and $4.1 million of interest, producing an $11.565 million net loss impact. Only approximately $1.8 million of penalties remains unrecorded. Even treating the recorded charge plus all stated penalties as a bridge deduction would reduce value by about $0.50 per share, small relative to the $8.82 gap between the $25.09 bull value and the $33.91 market price, so it cannot change the stated valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Confirm whether the $11.565 million charge remained payable at the valuation date and whether the $67.889 million cash balance was gross of settlement; deduct any unpaid amount once, include a probability-weighted penalty amount, and avoid double counting an amount already paid or captured in OE.

audit_findings.title: The valuation crosses a material insurance-contract boundary without updated terms
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; the filed renewal extends coverage through June 30, 2027, covers approximately 86% of exposure, and raises the disclosed return-premium range from $20-$30 million to $20-$32 million
audit_findings.mechanism: Renewal pricing, return-premium rights, retained risk, and collateral requirements affect future workers’ compensation expense, normalized OE, and potentially the cash bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: This fully insured arrangement covers claims incurred between July 1, 2021 and June 30, 2026.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest 10-Q demonstrates that the fully insured arrangement was renewed through June 30, 2027 and reports no retained claims risk for 2026, so expiration without replacement is not an open fact. However, the filing does not provide enough detail to compare premium pricing, collateral, and all economic terms with the prior arrangement. Because the renewed period began after the latest reported quarter and its effect is not yet present in filed operating results, this is a forward-looking monitoring item rather than a presently measurable valuation error.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the post-June 2026 policy terms and the first filed results under them; compare premiums, return-premium formulas, retentions, collateral, and termination rights with the prior contract, then rerun forward OE if the economics materially changed.
